title: Weak squares
line: Squares no enemy pawn can attack, and the knight that settles in one.

steps.text: Pawns never move back. Black's pawns on d5 and f5 have moved too far forward to guard the square between them.
A square no enemy pawn can attack is a weak square, or hole. Tap the hole in the center.
steps.hint: It is in Black's half, between two black pawns on the same row.
steps.after: No black pawn can attack it now.

steps.text: Put your knight in the hole. A piece there sits on an outpost: no black pawn can attack it there now.
steps.after: Black brings a knight to trade itself for yours.

steps.text: To be rid of your knight, Black would have to trade a piece for it. Its bishop on d6 guards the hole too.
Bring your bishop out to guard the knight. It also offers to trade Black's bishop, a guard of the hole.
steps.after: The knight is guarded, and the hole stays yours.

summary: Pawns never move back, so the squares they pass can be holes. Put a knight in one, where no enemy pawn can attack it.
